rules.defaultPosition: Provider (StrataNoble) retains all pre-existing IP, frameworks, methodologies, and reusable code components. Client receives a perpetual license to use pre-existing IP solely as incorporated into deliverables.

acceptableAlternatives.position: Shared ownership of novel innovations created specifically for the engagement
acceptableAlternatives.conditions: Only for truly novel innovations that could not have existed without this specific client relationship
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Requires separate IP addendum defining scope of shared IP

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: Client may request usage beyond deliverables for internal purposes only
acceptableAlternatives.notes: No sublicensing permitted; usage fee may apply

unacceptablePositions.position: Client owns all code and work product including frameworks and tools
unacceptablePositions.reason: Would prevent Provider from reusing core tools and methodologies on other projects

unacceptablePositions.position: Work-for-hire treatment of all engagement work
unacceptablePositions.reason: Incompatible with our business model; we invest in reusable frameworks

rules.notesForAI: Be firm on pre-existing IP retention. This is core to the business model. Frame as protecting the investment that allows us to deliver efficiently.

rules.defaultPosition: Client owns final deliverables (specific to their engagement) upon full payment. This includes custom configurations, client-specific logic, and branded assets.

acceptableAlternatives.position: Provider retains right to showcase work in portfolio (anonymized if requested)
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Client can request embargo period before portfolio use

unacceptablePositions.reason: Payment must be complete before IP transfer occurs

rules.notesForAI: Final deliverables ownership is typically negotiable. Focus on ensuring full payment is received before transfer.

rules.defaultPosition: Total liability capped at fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim. No liability for consequential, incidental, special, or punitive damages.

acceptableAlternatives.position: Cap at total contract value instead of 12-month lookback
acceptableAlternatives.conditions: For fixed-price engagements where total is clear upfront
acceptableAlternatives.notes: May be simpler for both parties to administer

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: Only with corresponding insurance coverage and premium pricing
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Requires escalation for approval of increased exposure

unacceptablePositions.reason: Uninsurable and existential risk to the business

unacceptablePositions.position: Liability for lost profits or business interruption
unacceptablePositions.reason: Consequential damages are unpredictable and potentially unlimited
Liability cap should at minimum cover what client paid

rules.escalationReason: Any deviation from standard liability cap requires leadership approval due to insurance and risk implications
rules.notesForAI: Liability is a hard negotiation point. Emphasize that our pricing assumes standard liability terms. Higher caps require premium pricing.

rules.defaultPosition: 25% deposit due upon signing, balance according to milestone schedule defined in SOW. Net 30 payment terms.

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: For established clients with payment history
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Document the client relationship justifying reduced deposit

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: For enterprise clients with standard procurement cycles
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Adjust project timeline accordingly to manage cash flow

unacceptablePositions.reason: Exposes Provider to significant delivery risk without payment protection
Creates cash flow strain and implies client solvency concerns
Payment should not depend on factors outside our control

rules.notesForAI: Deposit protects against scope changes and ensures client commitment. Be flexible on structure but maintain deposit requirement.

rules.defaultPosition: Either party may terminate for convenience with 30 days written notice. Client pays for work completed through termination date.

acceptableAlternatives.notes: Shorter notice is reasonable for shorter projects

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: For enterprise clients with complex transition needs
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Longer notice helps ensure orderly knowledge transfer

unacceptablePositions.position: Immediate termination without payment for work in progress
unacceptablePositions.reason: Provider must be compensated for completed work regardless of termination

unacceptablePositions.position: Termination penalties or clawbacks of already-paid fees
unacceptablePositions.reason: Fees for completed work are non-refundable

rules.notesForAI: Termination rights should be balanced. Focus on ensuring compensation for completed work rather than restricting termination rights.

rules.defaultPosition: Mutual confidentiality with 3-year survival period post-termination. Standard carve-outs for public information, prior knowledge, and independent development.

acceptableAlternatives.notes: Longer period is reasonable for regulated industries

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: Only for clearly designated trade secrets
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Trade secrets retain protection as long as they remain secret

unacceptablePositions.reason: Our methodologies and pricing are also confidential
Need ability to reference engagement existence at minimum

rules.notesForAI: Confidentiality terms are usually straightforward. Ensure mutual obligations and reasonable carve-outs for our portfolio.

rules.defaultPosition: Nevada law governs. Disputes resolved by mediation, then binding arbitration in Las Vegas. No jury trials.

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: Delaware is acceptable as a neutral, business-friendly jurisdiction
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Keep arbitration in Las Vegas if possible
May increase our costs for dispute resolution

unacceptablePositions.reason: Litigation is slower and more expensive than arbitration
Creates uncertainty and increased legal costs

rules.notesForAI: Nevada is strongly preferred. Arbitration protects both parties from expensive litigation. Be flexible on venue for good clients.

rules.defaultPosition: Provider uses AI-assisted coding tools as subprocessors. Human oversight applies to all AI outputs. AI tools are covered under confidentiality provisions.

acceptableAlternatives.position: Named disclosure of specific AI tools
acceptableAlternatives.conditions: For regulated industries requiring subprocessor identification
acceptableAlternatives.notes: List Claude, GitHub Copilot, or other tools used

unacceptablePositions.position: Complete prohibition of AI tool usage
unacceptablePositions.reason: AI tools are integral to our development process and efficiency

rules.notesForAI: AI disclosure is non-negotiable. We use AI tools and must disclose this. Focus on human oversight and confidentiality protections.

rules.defaultPosition: Mutual indemnification for third-party claims arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or IP infringement.

acceptableAlternatives.position: Broader indemnity for IP claims only
acceptableAlternatives.conditions: Provider may accept broader IP indemnity with proper insurance
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Ensure indemnity is limited to work created by Provider

unacceptablePositions.reason: Indemnity should be limited by the liability cap
Client responsible for materials they provide
Should have opportunity to cure before indemnity applies

rules.escalationReason: Indemnity changes may affect insurance coverage
rules.notesForAI: Indemnity should mirror liability limitations. Be careful about open-ended indemnification obligations.

rules.defaultPosition: 30-day warranty period. Deliverables will substantially conform to specifications. Remedy limited to repair or replacement.

acceptableAlternatives.conditions: For larger or more complex projects
For critical systems with specific SLA requirements
acceptableAlternatives.notes: May require additional fees to support extended warranty

unacceptablePositions.reason: Warranty should be limited to meeting documented specs
Cannot warranty items outside our control

rules.notesForAI: Warranty should be limited to documented specifications. Avoid open-ended performance guarantees.
